profile.summary: GeoDock predicts the structure of a two-chain protein complex from the structures of the two partners. It takes the sequences and structures of the docking partners, with no multiple sequence alignment, and returns a docked complex in which the residues are allowed to move, so conformational change on binding can be predicted rather than assumed away. The network is a multitrack iterative transformer, and the point of it is speed: the authors report an average inference time of under one second on a single GPU, which makes large-scale screening possible. On the DIPS test set they report a 43 per cent top-1 success rate, falling to 31 per cent after removing close homologs they found contaminating the standard training split.

summary_quotes.text: we present GeoDock, a multitrack iterative transformer network to predict a docked structure from separate docking partners
GeoDock inputs just the sequences and structures of the docking partners, which suits the tasks when the individual structures are given
GeoDock is flexible at the protein residue level, allowing the prediction of conformational changes upon binding.

GeoDock achieves a 43% top‐1 success rate, outperforming all other tested methods. However, in the standard DIPS train/test splits, we discovered contamination of close homologs in the training set. After decontaminating the training set, the success rate is 31%.
GeoDock attains an average inference speed of under one second on a single GPU, enabling its application in large-scale structure screening.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Conventional docking programs sample many candidate poses and rerank them, which is slow, and earlier deep learning dockers were faster but treated both partners as rigid bodies. GeoDock does neither. It is an iterative transformer over several tracks, taking the sequence and the structure of each partner, and it predicts the docked complex directly with residue-level flexibility. Because it takes structures rather than alignments, it fits the case where the individual structures are already known. The implementation depends on fair-esm, so language model embeddings of the sequences are part of the input pipeline. Inference is one call to a runner class with the two partner files.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One checkpoint ships in the repository, geodock/weights/dips_0.3.ckpt, about 51.8 MB, and the notebook loads it by that path. The package is geodock version 1.0.4 with Python 3.7 or newer and dependencies pinned as minimums: torch 2.0.1, pytorch-lightning 1.8.6, einops 0.6.0, biotite 0.37.0 and fair-esm 2.0.0. The checkpoint name refers to DIPS, the training set, and the 0.3 suffix is not explained in the sources read. A result should name the checkpoint and the package version, and should say whether the DIPS training split was decontaminated, because the paper reports success rates of 43 and 31 per cent for the same model on the contaminated and cleaned splits.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Supervised protein-protein docking model: a multitrack iterative transformer that predicts a two-chain complex from the two separate partners.

quotes.text: a multitrack iterative transformer network to predict a docked structure from separate docking partners
GeoDock is a novel multi-track iterative transformer network

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Multitrack iterative transformer with residue-level flexibility, using protein language model embeddings from fair-esm in the input pipeline. The sources read give no block or channel counts.

quotes.text: GeoDock is flexible at the protein residue level

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: Two structure files, one per docking partner, and an output name. No multiple sequence alignment is used. The notebook uploads partner1 and partner2 as files and passes their paths to the runner.

quotes.text: Unlike deep learning models for protein structure prediction that input multiple sequence alignments, GeoDock inputs just the sequences and structures of the docking partners

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: A PDB file of the docked complex, named after the out_name given to the runner, with chains A and B for the two partners. The notebook colours it by chain or by the B-factor column as lDDT.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not stated. The only size figure in the sources read is the checkpoint file, geodock/weights/dips_0.3.ckpt at 51,771,953 bytes.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: The Database of Interacting Protein Structures (DIPS), which the checkpoint name also records. The authors found close homologs contaminating the standard DIPS training split and report results before and after cleaning it. Evaluation also used DB5.5 and an antibody-antigen benchmark.

run_guide.summary: Install the package, clone the repository for the checkpoint, and dock two partner structures with the runner class.
prerequisites: Python 3.7 or newer, as setup.cfg requires.
A GPU with enough memory for the complex: the notebook's own warning is that some GPUs are too small for large complexes.
torch 2.0.1 or newer and the other pinned dependencies, which pip installs with the package.
MIT terms for the code. The checkpoint is committed in the same repository, with no separate licence statement.

steps.title: Clone the repository at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/Graylab/GeoDock.git
cd GeoDock
git checkout --detach df8d1f4c24ae2946655f27e7411ba2ffabf3d350
steps.explanation: The clone is needed for the checkpoint, which is committed at geodock/weights/dips_0.3.ckpt; the checkout line pins the commit that was read. The notebook does the same clone inside Colab.
steps.source_locator: repository listing: weights; GeoDock.ipynb: Run Prediction cell

steps.title: Install the package
steps.shell:
pip install geodock
pip install torch-geometric
pip install torch-scatter -f https://pytorch-geometric.com/whl/torch-${TORCH}+${CUDA}.html
pip install torch-sparse -f https://pytorch-geometric.com/whl/torch-${TORCH}+${CUDA}.html
pip install torch-cluster -f https://pytorch-geometric.com/whl/torch-${TORCH}+${CUDA}.html
pip install torch-spline-conv -f https://pytorch-geometric.com/whl/torch-${TORCH}+${CUDA}.html
steps.explanation: The notebook's install cell. Beyond the geodock package, which declares torch, pytorch-lightning, einops, biotite and fair-esm in setup.cfg, the cell installs torch-geometric and the matching torch-scatter, torch-sparse, torch-cluster and torch-spline-conv wheels, with TORCH and CUDA set from the installed torch build. The notebook also installs py3Dmol, which is only needed for its 3D viewer.
steps.source_locator: GeoDock.ipynb: Install dependencies cell; setup.cfg: install_requires

steps.title: Dock two partners
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from geodock.GeoDockRunner import GeoDockRunner

ckpt_file = "geodock/weights/dips_0.3.ckpt"
geodock = GeoDockRunner(ckpt_file=ckpt_file)
pred = geodock.dock(
    partner1="partner1.pdb",
    partner2="partner2.pdb",
    out_name="test",
    do_refine=False,
    use_openmm=True,
)
PY
steps.explanation: The notebook's prediction cell, wrapped here in a shell heredoc, with the checkpoint path made relative to the clone and the two uploaded files replaced by local file names. do_refine is False because the notebook says refinement is not yet supported.

notes: The record came from the antibody-antigen affinity evaluation framework (existing source lit-interactions-20261011-mochibind-source-isci2026). GeoDock is a general two-chain docking model, not an affinity predictor: it returns a structure, and any affinity number in a benchmark comes from something built on top of it. The paper's own abstract reports that GeoDock falls behind most conventional methods and behind AlphaFold-Multimer on the antibody-antigen benchmark, which is worth noting for a record that reached us through an antibody-antigen study. Only the abstract is openly available for the paper, so coverage is marked limited. The README contains no usage instructions; the run guide comes from the repository's Colab notebook. No saved file states a licence for the committed checkpoint, so weights_licence is null; the repository itself is MIT.
